record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the n-city travelling salesman path problem with cities 1 through n, a start at city 1, an end at city n, distances d(i, j), and the goal of visiting cities 2 through n-1 in some order while minimizing total path length, construct an exact algorithm running in O*(1.99^n) time, where O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Construct an exact algorithm for the n-city TSP with O*(1.99n) time complexity!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let d : {1,…,n} × {1,…,n} → ℝ_{≥0} be a distance function (not assumed symmetric or to satisfy the triangle inequality). Consider the Hamiltonian-path version of the travelling salesman problem: among all permutations σ of {2,…,n−1}, find one minimizing

  d(1, σ(2)) + d(σ(2), σ(3)) + ⋯ + d(σ(n−2), σ(n−1)) + d(σ(n−1), n),

i.e., the shortest path starting at city 1, ending at city n, and visiting each of the cities 2,…,n−1 exactly once.

Design an exact algorithm that solves this problem in time O*(1.99^n), where O*(·) suppresses factors polynomial in n (and in the bit-length of the input distances). Equivalently, exhibit a constant c < 2 and an exact algorithm running in time O*(c^n).
artifact.status_search_result: The classical Bellman–Held–Karp dynamic programming algorithm has run in O*(2^n) time for over sixty years. Recent work (e.g., a 2024 result by Stoian) improves the running time only by a sub-polynomial factor of the form 2^n · n^2 / 2^Ω(√log n), via faster min-plus matrix multiplication. No algorithm running in O*(c^n) with a constant c < 2 (such as 1.99^n) is known for general TSP, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: TSP Escapes the O(2^n n^2) Curse
status_evidence.snippet: The dynamic programming solution to the traveling salesman problem due to Bellman, and Held and Karp, runs in time O(2^n n^2), with no improvement in the last sixty years. We design an algorithm running in deterministic time 2^n n^2 / 2^Ω(√log n).
status_evidence.claim: State of the art improvement over Held–Karp is only sub-polynomial, leaving sub-2^n constant-base running time open.

status_evidence.title: Held–Karp algorithm - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Held–Karp algorithm solves TSP in time O(n^2 2^n).
status_evidence.claim: Baseline exact TSP complexity is O*(2^n).
